Findings demonstrate that cloud water exploitation significantly alleviates engineering-induced shortages and ecological water competition, supporting climate adaptation and sustainable water management.

title: Machine learning gap-filling of hydrometeorological time series in south-central Chile: Streamflow, temperature and precipitation
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Paul Sandoval-Quilodrán, Guillermo Barrientos, Johan Valdés, Isadora León-Soto, Piero Mardones, Efrain Duarte, Pedro Arriagada, Mauricio Aguayo, Rafael Rubilar
abstract: Study Region This study was conducted in south-central Chile, between 34°S and 41°S, encompassing a hydroclimatically diverse region extending from the Pacific coast to the Andes Mountains. Study Focus We evaluated the non-parametric MissForest algorithm for gap-filling daily hydrometeorological time series from 1980 to 2022 across 57 streamflow, 19 temperature, and 97 precipitation stations with < 20% missing data. Performance was assessed under point and continuous-gap validation schemes using the modified Kling–Gupta Efficiency (KGE), root mean square error (RMSE), and, for precipitation, wet-day occurrence diagnostics. For meteorological variables, ERA5-Land was also evaluated both as an auxiliary predictor within the MissForest framework and as input to a linear regression baseline. New Hydrological Insights for the Region MissForest improved moderately incomplete hydrometeorological records; however, performance depended on variable type and gap structure. Point gaps were reconstructed more accurately than continuous gaps, with median observation-based KGE decreasing from 0.89 ± 0.11–0.66 ± 0.43. Temperature exhibited the most stable performance, whereas precipitation remained sensitive to wet-day occurrence and event timing. Streamflow showed the greatest variability under continuous validation, particularly during high-flow conditions. ERA5-Land enhanced meteorological gap-filling primarily under point validation, yielding near-optimal KGE values for temperature and precipitation while reducing false wet days. Overall, MissForest is most suitable for short, isolated gaps and general daily variability, whereas caution is needed for extremes events and long continuous gaps.

title: An analytical study on the influence of initial soil moisture and meteorological anomalies on flash droughts
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Vishal Singh, Tushar Apurv
abstract: Study region The study focusses on 13 major watersheds of India. Study focus Rapid depletion of soil moisture during flash droughts is influenced by complex interactions between initial soil moisture and anomalies in meteorological variables. In this study, numerical experiments are conducted on an analytical land-atmospheric model to gain a conceptual understanding of the influence of initial soil moisture (SM) and meteorological anomalies on flash droughts. The analytical model is calibrated using reanalysis dataset and validated with remotely sensed surface soil moisture. Numerical experiments are conducted on the calibrated model by perturbing the soil moisture at the onset of flash drought events and its impact on flash drought severity are analysed. New hydrological insights for the region It is found that the influence of meteorological anomalies decreases with initial soil moisture in majority of monsoon season flash droughts in humid, sub-humid and semi-arid regions. In these flash droughts, precipitation anomalies are the major contributors to flash droughts. On the other hand, the influence of meteorological anomalies increases with initial soil moisture in flash droughts of arid regions. In these flash droughts, soil moisture depletion is primarily driven by precipitation anomalies in dry antecedent conditions and jointly by precipitation and potential evapotranspiration anomalies in wet antecedent conditions. The insights gained from the analysis highlight the need to use region- and season-specific predictors for accurate prediction of flash drought severity.

title: A hybrid modeling approach for analyzing the risk propagation of water quality deterioration associated with water transfer during flood season
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Rui Yang, Wenlong Chen, Yiping Li, Qiong Wu, Xudong Li, Shiqiang Wu, Chen Zhang
abstract: Study region The Nansi Lake is a key storage reservoir for the Eastern Route of the South-to-North Water Diversion Project in China. Study focus As a new practice in existing water diversion projects, inter-basin water transfer during flood season poses new challenges to water quality deterioration risk management. Risk propagation analysis is crucial for risk management, which constitutes a critical determinant for the success of flood-season water transfer operations. Commonly used risk propagation analysis models in water quality deterioration, such as the hydrodynamic-water quality model or data-driven models, either fail to quantify the probability and magnitude of risk propagation, or are limited by insufficient risk associated records. Therefore, a new hybrid modeling approach is designed to overcome the limitations, coupling a Hydrodynamic-water quality model, a C-Vine Copula function, Sine functions, and a Markov chain. It can depict the physical and stochastic processes of water quality deterioration risk, further deciphering its spatial evolution pattern. New hydrological insights for the region The results show that 33∼67% of the lake area is highly likely (97.5%) to suffer water quality deterioration when water transfer scheduled during flood season, and the middle and northern regions of the lake are the hotspots of high risk. Moreover, the risk propagation route is from rivers to the lake and from the south to the north in the lake. From the spatial risk evolution perspective, it maintains low-risk or medium-risk propagation in the south, while exhibiting risk-enhanced propagation in the middle, and maintaining high-risk propagation in the north. Thus, rivers flowing into the north and middle of the lake are the priorities for the risk management. Overall, the study quantitatively reveal the spatiotemporal evolution patterns of water quality deterioration risk, identifying risk hotspots in the lake and the priority areas for risk management. These results provide decision-makers with a scientific basis for optimizing water environment management strategies.

title: The Altered Water Balance: An analysis of urban shallow groundwater level dynamics using a high-density groundwater level observation network for Aalborg, Denmark
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Søren Thorndahl, Per Møldrup, Ida Kemppinen Vester, Jesper Ellerbæk Nielsen, Morten Westergaard, Anja Sloth Ziegler
abstract: Study Region: The research is conducted in the Kærby district of Aalborg, Denmark (0.6 km 2 ). Study Focus: Urban areas with shallow groundwater levels face increasing challenges related to groundwater flooding, infrastructure damage, and sewer system infiltration under changing anthropogenic climatic conditions. This study aims to quantify and analyze components of the water balance through a comprehensive, observation-based assessment of shallow urban groundwater variability, using high-resolution data from both citizen science initiatives and automated groundwater level monitoring. New Hydrological Insights for the Region: Over a 4.5-year period, groundwater levels are monitored, revealing seasonal fluctuations of approximately ± 0 . 5 m, and rapid dynamic responses to individual rainfall events, with observed groundwater level increases up to 6 times the corresponding rainfall depth. Cross-correlation analysis links fluctuations to antecedent precipitation and groundwater recharge dynamics. Hydraulic characterization indicates high infiltrability and a narrow vadose zone (0–2 m), explaining rapid saturation and groundwater response. The study quantifies groundwater infiltration into combined sewers using a water budget, showing that in some subcatchments, annual infiltration matches precipitation and exceeds recharge, suggesting lateral inflow and anthropogenically transformed flow regimes. Geospatial interpolation reveals inverted gradients and lowered groundwater levels driven by infrastructure-induced drainage. The study reveals a natural water balance altered by urbanization. The findings highlight the importance of understanding natural and anthropogenic hydrological processes to support climate-resilient urban water management and inform solutions mitigating groundwater impacts.

title: Spatiotemporal propagation of multi-type droughts across different ecological geographical regions in China: Explaining the contributions of atmospheric teleconnection factors
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Tingting Wang, Ni Wang, Jiancang Xie, Ganggang Zuo, Xinyue Ke, Xixi Lv
abstract: Study region The study region is China's four major ecological geographical regions Study focus Investigating the cascading propagation effects of different drought types across distinct zones and their influence by atmospheric circulation is crucial for refined regional water resource management. This study systematically characterizes meteorological, hydrological, and ecological droughts. By constructing a comprehensive analytical framework integrating Pearson correlation analysis, wavelet coherence, and interpretable machine learning, we quantified the spatiotemporal coherence of multi-type drought evolution, propagation delays, and the nonlinear driving effects of atmospheric circulation factors. New hydrological insights for the region (1)The propagation of meteorological drought to hydrological drought is significant on the long timescale, while its progression to ecological drought is concentrated on the shorter timescale. (2)Meteorological and hydrological droughts in China's northwest region have continued to worsen, while ecological drought conditions have eased. (3)Hydrological drought follows a meteorological cascade with lags ranging from near-synchronous to approximately 1.5 months. Conversely, ecological drought exhibits decoupling and weaker correlations, manifesting as quasi-instantaneous responses in islands. (4)Among atmospheric circulation factors, ENSO dominates meteorological drought, while sunspot activity emerges as a key associated factor, producing opposing effects. These findings clarify the distinct propagation lags and atmospheric forcing mechanisms across diverse drought types.

title: Integrated geophysical and hydrochemical characterization of geologically and structurally complex groundwater systems in the Mekelle area, northern Ethiopia
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Kaleab Adhena Abera, Yonatan Garkabo Doyoro, Tesfamichael Gebreyohannes, Miruts Hagos, Gebremedhin Berhane, Abdelwassie Hussien, Marieke Paepen, Thomas Hermans, Kristine Walraevens
abstract: Study region Mekelle area, northern Ethiopia. Study focus Groundwater in sedimentary basins is influenced by lithology and structural deformation, yet these controls remain poorly understood in many sedimentary basins. This study investigates subsurface architecture and groundwater characteristics using an integrated geophysical and hydrochemical approach. Vertical electrical soundings (VES, DC resistivity method), supported by borehole lithological logs, were used to delineate subsurface units and structures. Major-ion chemistry of 107 groundwater and surface water samples was analyzed to identify hydrochemical facies, water–rock interactions, and anthropogenic influences. New hydrological insights for the region Integrated geophysical and hydrochemical results indicate a structurally controlled, heterogeneous aquifer system with pronounced hydraulic compartmentalization. Geophysical evidence shows that dolerite intrusions mainly behave as resistive units that locally restrict groundwater flow but also serve as productive aquifers where sufficiently fractured. Fault and fracture networks enhance secondary permeability and form preferential groundwater pathways that control aquifer connectivity. Hydrochemical data reflect this structural control, with shallow groundwater dominated by Ca–HCO₃ and Ca–Mg–HCO₃ facies, indicating active recharge conditions. In contrast, Ca–SO₄ facies in deeper groundwater are linked to interaction with gypsum-bearing formations. Elevated nitrate and chloride concentrations in shallow groundwater further indicate influence from surface-derived contamination. These findings demonstrate the strong influence of lithology and structural features on groundwater systems and support improved groundwater management in complex sedimentary basins.

title: Understanding temperature-driven drought intensification in Northeast Asia through multiple drought indices
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Ghani Rahman, Umar Farooq, Subin Kang, Joo-Heon Lee, Hyun-Han Kwon
abstract: Study region Northeast Asia encompasses diverse hydroclimatic conditions across nine Köppen climate zones. Study focus This study investigates the spatiotemporal dynamics of drought intensification in Northeast Asia (NEA) using the Standardized Precipitation Index (SPI), the Standardized Precipitation-Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI), and the Evaporative Demand Drought Index (EDDI). We apply a multi-index framework with General Linear Modeling (GLM) to assess the effects of climatic variables on drought severity. Drought characteristics are assessed at 1-, 3-, 6-, and 12-month timescales using ERA5 reanalysis data from 1974 to 2023. New hydrological insights Trend analysis reveals a shift from seasonal droughts before 2004 to prolonged events. Northern China and Mongolia emerge as major long-term drought hotspots. SPEI and EDDI consistently display greater sensitivity to temperature-driven droughts than SPI. GLM analysis shows that minimum temperature has the strongest association with drought intensification (η²p = 0.046–0.105), followed by dewpoint temperature (η²p = 0.037–0.077). EDDI demonstrates the highest sensitivity in minimum temperature (η²p = 0.105), whereas SPI exhibits the weakest response (η²p = 0.046). Rising temperature and solar radiation intensify droughts, while higher dewpoint temperature reduces severity. These findings indicate that drought intensification in NEA is primarily associated with interacting temperature and energy-related processes rather than precipitation alone. This multi-index, climate-stratified approach provides a mechanistic understanding of water–energy interactions driving drought variability, supporting monitoring and adaptive water management under climate change.

title: Beyond static DPSIR: A CDPSIR-path dependency synthesis explaining 60 Years of groundwater policy failure in Rafsanjan, Iran
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Elham Golkar, Ali Bagheri
abstract: Study region The Rafsanjan Plain aquifer in arid south‑eastern Iran (rainfall: 137 mm/year) has been a “forbidden plain” since 1974. Despite five decades of policies, groundwater levels declined 23.5 m (1983–2019), with extraction (∼683 MCM/year) far exceeding recharge (∼432 MCM/year). Pistachio cultivation (∼80,000–100,000 ha) accounts for ∼503 MCM/year of extraction. Study focus Why have all policies since 1966 failed to halt decline? Moving beyond static assessments, we conduct a root‑cause analysis using a novel synthesis: Grounded Theory within an extended CDPSIR (Context‑Driving Forces‑Pressures‑State‑Impacts‑Responses) framework, combined with path dependency theory and causal loop diagrams. We trace 160 years (1861–present) across five periods to identify critical junctures, self‑reinforcing mechanisms, and lock‑in effects. New hydrological insights for the region The crisis is not a technical failure but path‑dependent lock‑in from export‑oriented pistachio monoculture. Five critical junctures (1861 cotton boom, 1921 pistachio transition, 1962 Land Reform, 1979 Revolution, 1982 Fair Water Distribution Law) activated self‑reinforcing mechanisms—increasing returns, learning, coordination, adaptive expectations, institutional complementarity, and technological lock‑in—that raised deviation costs. By the 1980s, only wells running dry provided any corrective force. Past policies (drip irrigation, forbidden plain, legalization amnesties) failed because they were overwhelmed by lock‑in structures. We derive transferable conditions and propose agrivoltaics on non‑productive orchards to break the lock‑in.

title: A physics-informed data-driven framework for 30m soil moisture estimation from multi-source datasets
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Yixin Jiang, Jun Zhang, Ziyi Cai, Yulin Chen, Sa Wei, Miao Liu, Ze Jiang, Yy Yi Liu, Wenchao Ma
abstract: Study region Hebei Plain, Hebei Province, China. Study focus Accurate, high-resolution soil moisture (SM) estimation is crucial for field-scale hydrological modeling, agricultural management, and climate research, yet current approaches remain limited by sparse in situ observations and coarse spatial resolution of satellite-based products. To address these challenges, this study develops a robust physics-informed data-driven framework for estimating 0–10 cm SM at 30 m resolution by integrating multi-source datasets through spatiotemporal data fusion and machine learning models. New hydrological insights The proposed framework consists of three key methodological advances. First, to bridge the spatial resolution gap and ensure high-quality inputs, we systematically evaluated four spatiotemporal data fusion algorithms, identifying Enhanced Spatial and Temporal Adaptive Reflectance Fusion Model (ESTARFM) as superior for maintaining consistent spectral and spatial representation of surface reflectance and temperature at 30 m resolution, achieving the highest r and the lowest RMSE, EDGE and LBP values across most cities. Second, we constructed a hybrid feature set coupling physically interpretable indices, such as the Temperature Vegetation Dryness Index (TVDI), with multi-source reanalysis and topographic data, ensuring an efficient predictor set through multicollinearity diagnosis. Third, using Optuna-driven automated hyperparameter optimization, we benchmarked ten machine-learning algorithms, finding that Random Forest (RF) exhibited the most robust performance with r of 0.921, R² of 0.835, RMSE of 2.512% and near-zero bias (−0.041%) against in situ SM observations. The resulting 30 m soil moisture maps effectively resolve fine-scale landscape heterogeneity. Overall, this study provides a robust, scalable, and application-ready ML-based framework for generating SM products with high spatiotemporal resolution, offering valuable support for regional water resource management and drought monitoring in complex agricultural landscapes.

title: Graph transformer-based flood susceptibility mapping: Application to the French Riviera and railway infrastructure under climate change
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Sreenath Vemula, Filippo Gatti, Pierre Jehel
abstract: Study region The French Riviera watershed in southeastern France (≈2650 km²) extends from steep alpine headwaters to a densely urbanised Mediterranean coast traversed by the SNCF rail network, and has suffered repeated destructive floods, including the 1994 and 2010 Var floods, the 2015 Côte d’Azur flood, and the 2020 Storm Alex. Study focus Traditional machine-learning (ML) approaches achieve high point-wise metrics (AUC-ROC, accuracy) but fail to produce the spatially coherent predictions needed for reliable infrastructure-exposure estimation. We propose a graph transformer (GT) architecture incorporating a feature-similarity graph regularised by Laplacian positional encodings and spatial attention, and benchmark it against six traditional ML models, and show that these point-wise metrics alone are insufficient and should be complemented by spatial autocorrelation metrics (Moran's I, Geary's C) when evaluating multi-class flood predictions. Using topographic, hydrologic, and environmental features, we further project flood susceptibility and railway-track exposure for 2050 under RCP 4.5 and RCP 8.5 scenarios. New hydrological insights for the region The GT achieved AUC-ROC ≈ 0.974 (slightly below XGBoost ≈ 0.990) but substantially improved spatial coherence (Moran’s I ≈ 0.612, Geary’s C ≈ 0.473 versus XGBoost 0.409 and 0.589, and RF 0.474 and 0.523). Its smooth boundary delineation produced markedly different distributions: the GT classified 6.2% of the area as very-high with 35.6% railway exposure, versus 55–57% very-high area and 46–52% railway exposure for ML models; the GT very-high extent closely matches the 172.6 km² historical inundation inventory. Accumulated Local Effects analysis confirmed elevation, stream power, and precipitation as dominant monotonic drivers consistent with flood hydrology. Scenario-conditional projections for 2050 under RCP 4.5 (Q95) and RCP 8.5 (Q95) indicate very-high areas could expand to ≈ 28% and ≈ 36.3%, with railway exposure reaching ≈ 64% and ≈ 67.4%. The GT framework provides a replicable blueprint for regions seeking spatially accurate flood susceptibility mapping.

title: Prediction of regional water and land resource carrying capacity using support vector machines supported by Monte Carlo coupled black-winged kite optimization algorithm
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Kun Cheng, Xingyang Zhang, Nan Sun, Bao Zhu
abstract: Study region Heilongjiang Province in Northeast China. Study focus Studies on the carrying capacity of water and land resources (WLRCC) provide a critical basis for achieving the efficient use of these resources in the region. Traditional forecasting methods only calculate specific values at a single point in the future, failing to reflect the uncertainty of future water and land resource carrying capacity. Furthermore, the classification criteria for water and land resource carrying capacity are neither comprehensive nor accurate. To address these issues, this study employs a combined objective-subjective approach to establish classification criteria and proposes a forecasting method based on the coupling of Monte Carlo simulation with the Black Kite algorithm to optimize support vector machines, thereby resolving the issue of one-dimensional forecasting results for regional water and land resource carrying capacity. New hydrological insights for the region The carrying capacity of water and land resources in Heilongjiang Province will continue to show an overall upward trend from 2030 to 2040. Concurrently, the standard deviation—a measure of system variability—will increase significantly, with Jiamusi, Shuangyashan, and Qitaihe exhibiting the most pronounced increases, with standard deviation growth rates reaching 288%, 283%, and 198%, respectively. The findings of this study can provide guidance for the management and development of regional water and land resources.

title: Benchmark-guided insights into hybrid process-based-deep learning models for continental-scale streamflow prediction across the United States
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Daneti Arun Sourya, Velpuri Manikanta, Maheswaran Rathinasamy
abstract: Study region United States of America (USA) Study focus Recent studies have explored hybrid process-based (PB) - deep learning (DL) approaches, yet it remains unclear when hybridisation is necessary and whether it systematically improves performance across diverse catchments. To address this, we propose a benchmark-guided evaluation framework applied to 531 U.S. catchments. A suite of 17 simple benchmark (BM) models was used to establish a catchment-specific performance critical range based on modified Kling-Gupta Efficiency (KGE). Models exceeding the benchmark were classified as skilful, while those below were considered underperforming. This study identifies catchments where PB hydrological models outperform BM expectations, while DL, i.e., long short-term memory (LSTM) model, underperform relative to BM expectations. For these catchments, we investigate whether integrating PB model outputs of soil moisture (SM) and/or discharge (Q) into LSTM architectures improves streamflow simulation. The objective is to determine under which catchment conditions hybrid PB-LSTM configurations provide measurable performance gains and which PB-derived inputs are most effective. New hydrological insights for the region The hybrid configurations produced clear improvements over standalone LSTMs, with nearly 30% of catchments shifting from fair to good performance categories. Feature importance analysis indicates that PB-derived SM consistently enhances prediction skill by improving representation of hydrologic memory and subsurface dynamics. These results demonstrate that benchmark-guided hybridisation provides a systematic and interpretable strategy for improving data-driven streamflow modelling across diverse hydroclimatic conditions.

title: Three decades of high-Arctic river monitoring revealed no trend in runoff and a regime shift in glacial lake outburst floods
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Daniel Binder, Kirsty Langley, Signe Hillerup Larsen, Mikhail Mastepanov, Jakob Abermann, Michele Citterio, Eva P.S. Eibl, Arno C. Hammann, Bernhard Hynek, Kristian Kjellerup Kjeldsen, Daniel Alexander Rudd, Wolfgang Schöner, Kirstine Skov, Erik V. Sørensen, Mikkel Tamstorf
abstract: Study region Zackenberg River Catchment, NE-Greenland. Study focus Arctic freshwater runoff has increased due to rising air temperatures, and associated increases in precipitation and ice melt. While the runoff of river catchments connected to the Greenland Ice Sheet has increased, there is no clear signal for catchments disconnected from the ice sheet. Here, we analyze the Zackenberg River discharge record, the longest record from a Greenlandic river catchment disconnected from the ice sheet. New hydrological insights for the region We find no significant long-term trend in river runoff and explain this by the limited glacier coverage of the catchment, while precipitation as the primary driver shows no trend. Since monitoring began in 1996, recurrent flood waves originating from the outburst of a glacier-dammed lake have been observed. Their already moderate contribution to annual runoff has recently begun to diminish, accompanied by a change of flood characteristics. Continued glacier mass loss acted as long-term preconditioning factor for the shift in outburst characteristics. We show that prior to the shift, rapid subglacial lake drainages dominated, with timing linked to the seasonal development of the subglacial drainage system. The onset of ice dam disintegration in 2019 initiated a transition to ice-marginal dominated flood routing with declining lake drainage rates and volumes. We present a conceptual model for this new drainage dynamics and propose that it will ultimately lead to ice dam collapse and the cessation of the outburst floods.

title: Low-flow patterns and hydrological regionalisation across the Baltic Sea basin
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): S. Nazarenko, D. Meilutytė-Lukauskienė, V. Akstinas, P. Marcinkowski, A. Sharifi, A. Torabi Haghighi, Y. Kobets, A. Reihan, I. Kokorīte, L. Bērtiņa, C. Teutschbein
abstract: Study region The Baltic Sea basin covers approximately 1.7 million km² across northern Europe, extending from sub-Arctic to temperate climates with pronounced gradients in snow cover, precipitation, temperature, and catchment storage. As one of the largest brackish sea basins globally, its hydrology regulates freshwater and nutrient inputs that critically influence coastal water quality and marine ecosystem functioning. Despite its ecological and hydrological importance, a consistent basin-scale assessment of low-flow regimes across national boundaries has been lacking, with existing studies limited to individual countries using different methods and indicators. Study focus The study analyses daily discharge records from 134 water gauging stations across six countries (Sweden, Finland, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, and Poland) for the period 1961–2020. Low-flow conditions were characterised using the annual minimum 30-day mean discharge (Q30) and its catchment-area-normalised form of specific discharge (q30), enabling comparison of low-flow magnitude, seasonality, and variability, across contrasting hydroclimatic regions. We examined spatial patterns, temporal changes between two climate normal periods (1961–1990 and 1991–2020), and identified hydrologically coherent regions through K-means cluster analysis based on q30, coefficient of variation, proportion of warm-season low-flow, and mean catchment elevation. New hydrological insights Low-flow magnitude shows a pronounced spatial dipole: q30 increased by 20–65% in high-latitude and mountainous catchments, while mid-latitude lowlands experienced declines of –10 to –30%, particularly in Poland and the Baltic States. A well-defined latitudinal transition around 61.8°N separates cold-season (snow-dominated) from warm-season (rainfall-dominated) low-flow regimes. Between the two periods, mid-latitude basins underwent a near-complete shift towards warm-season low-flow dominance, consistent with earlier snowmelt and increased evapotranspiration. Cluster analysis identified six coherent low-flow regime types that align with major climatic and physiographic gradients. While the regional structure remained stable, 40 stations (29.9%) changed cluster membership, concentrated in transitional mid-latitude zones. These findings provide the first basin-scale regionalisation of low-flow regimes in the Baltic Sea basin and offer a quantitative framework for transboundary drought screening and climate adaptation planning.

title: Spatio-temporal patterns and driving factors of the compound drought and heatwave events across the Yellow River Basin
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Yifan Zou, Xiaomeng Song, Xiaojun Wang, Jianyun Zhang
abstract: Study area The Yellow River Basin (YRB), China Study focus Climate change has increased the occurrence of extreme climate events worldwide, particularly compound drought and heatwave events (CDHE). The YRB is an ecologically sensitive area that plays a crucial role in supporting industrial and agricultural activities in China. Thus, it is essential to conduct a comprehensive study on CDHE in the YRB. New hydrological insights for the region This study developed a compound drought and heatwave magnitude index (CDHMI) using meteorological data to investigate the historical changes in CDHE within the YRB. Additionally, we examined the relationships between drought and heatwaves in CDHE, exploring their contributing factors and potential influences. Lastly, we combined CMIP6 models to assess their applicability to the YRB and projected future changes in CDHE. The results show that: (1) CDHE is more likely to occur in the middle and lower reaches of the YRB, with a mean frequency and duration of 1.09 events/year and 5.12 days/year, respectively. (2) Droughts and heatwaves in the YRB are generally positively correlated, and the connection between droughts and heatwaves is strengthening, especially in duration. The contribution of CDHE is primarily influenced by heatwaves, with ET being the key factor affecting CDHE, accounting for 20.6 ± 0.79% of the relative importance. (3) There are notable differences in CDHE among the 23 different global climate models, with the INM-CM4–8 being optimally modelled at YRB, followed by FGOALS-g3. CDHE significantly increased with rising SSP, with the largest magnitude in the SSP5–8.5 scenario.

title: Increased soil moisture dominates the prolongation of leaf longevity for alpine grasslands in the Three-River-Source Region
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Yuxi Wang, Lin Zhang
abstract: Study regions The Three-River-Source Region Study focus This study integrated multi-source remote sensing and flux data from 2003 to 2022 to analyze the spatiotemporal dynamics of grassland leaf longevity (LL) and moisture conditions in the Three-River-Source Region. By applying a binning-based decoupling approach, we successfully isolated the independent impacts of soil moisture (SM) and vapor pressure deficit (VPD). New hydrological insights for the region Nearly half the region experienced intensified water stress, expanding warm-season compound droughts. Initially, LL correlated positively with SM and negatively with VPD in most regions, masking their distinct roles. Decoupling revealed SM as the dominant regulatory factor for LL, contributing approximately threefold more than VPD. The widely reported inhibitory effect of atmospheric dryness on grassland phenology was strongly amplified by its collinearity with soil aridity, with the role of VPD became more prominent when SM exceeded the non-restrictive threshold. Spatially, cold-region LL was more sensitive to soil-atmosphere moisture shifts, while in semi-humid regions, SM change still dominated, but VPD stress grew. These findings clarify the distinct mechanisms of soil-atmosphere moisture impacts, highlighting the importance of decoupling methods for ecological regulation analysis and guide adaptive ecological management.

title: Improving regional low-flow modeling in ungauged French catchments using the SMASH platform: A comparative assessment of grid-based parsimonious GR hydrological models and ANN-based regionalization strategies
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Thomas de Fournas, Nathalie Folton, Ngo Nghi Truyen Huynh, François Colleoni, Pierre-André Garambois
abstract: Study region 248 French catchments. Study focus Accurate streamflow prediction in ungauged basins requires parsimonious model structures and efficient optimization strategies. Using the SMASH (Spatially distributed Modeling and ASsimilation for Hydrology) framework, we performed a comparative evaluation of three spatially distributed, parsimonious GR-like hydrological models. We investigated the influence of three regional calibration strategies—Uniform, Multi-Linear regression, and Artificial Neural Networks (ANN)—to regionalize spatially distributed conceptual parameters using physical descriptors. The primary focus is assessing model transferability to ungauged basins, with particular attention to accurately reproducing low-flow indicators critical for drought monitoring and water resource management. New hydrological insights for the region Within the SMASH framework, regionalized models based on artificial neural networks (ANN) exhibit substantial gains in predictive accuracy compared to spatially uniform calibration. In temporal validation, the parsimonious distributed models (LoiEau and GR4) coupled with ANN achieved the highest robustness, reaching a median NSE(1/Q) of 0.60 (improving by +0.22 over uniform calibration). Furthermore, the added value of the distributed SMASH framework is substantial in challenging ungauged basin conditions (spatio-temporal validation). Benchmarked against the Lumped_LoiEau baseline, SMASH-ANN (LoiEau) improves the median NSE(√Q) from 0.57 to 0.75. This advantage is even more pronounced for low flows: SMASH-ANN (LoiEau) achieves a median NSE(1/Q) of 0.45, outperforming both the lumped baseline (+0.25 over the lumped model's 0.20) and the more complex distributed GR5 model (0.38). Beyond these goodness-of-fit improvements, the spatially distributed parameter fields provide physically coherent representations of French regional hydrology. The ANN mapping autonomously extracts complex groundwater interactions, accurately capturing flow losses to deep aquifers in chalk-dominated systems (e.g., Seine-Normandy). However, the study also highlights the physical limits of regionalization: in severely data-scarce environments (Mediterranean and Uniform regimes), extreme low flows are governed by localized hydrogeological features, causing descriptor-based mappings to overfit.

title: Hydraulic response of a river reach supplying urban water under extreme drought conditions
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Lucas Vinicius Dias, Camila Hamano Toledo, Lais Ferrer Amorim de Oliveira, Paulo Fernando Soares, Cláudia Telles Benatti
abstract: Study region Pirapó River Basin in Paraná State, southern Brazil, is a surface-water-dependent system that supplies the city of Maringá through a 90 km river reach from headwaters to main intake. Study focus This study investigates how hydrological drought propagates into hydraulic conditions along a river channel and affects water availability for urban supply. A one-dimensional hydraulic model (HEC-RAS) was developed using channel geometry derived from DEM correction and field bathymetric surveys. Model calibration was performed using Manning’s roughness coefficients and evaluated using deterministic metrics, event-based low-flow statistics, and residual-based uncertainty analysis. Historical drought scenarios (2000–2020) were simulated to assess low-flow hydraulic behavior along the river. New hydrological insights for the region Results show that drought conditions do not translate uniformly along the river but instead generate strong spatial heterogeneity in hydraulic response. During severe drought events, more than 45% of the 90 km reach exhibits discharges below 2 m³ s⁻¹, with upstream and midstream sections experiencing critical flow reductions, while downstream reaches partially recover due to cumulative inflows. These findings demonstrate that basin-scale discharge indicators alone are insufficient to assess water supply reliability, as hydraulic conditions controlling abstraction are spatially variable. Despite uncertainties in groundwater contributions and withdrawals, the main hydraulic patterns remain robust. Results highlight the importance of integrating reach-scale hydraulic modeling into water resource management to support drought resilience planning.

title: Hydrological amplification effect of pollutant flux in rivers discharging to the sea under climate change
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Huaixing Wang, Shengtian Yang, Hezhen Lou, Aiping Feng, Wenlong Song, Xuelei Wang, Baichi Zhou, Jiyi Gong, Yulian Wang, Gaohu Sun, Xin Zhang
abstract: Study region The Luanhe River Basin (LRB) in northern China. Study focus Climate change has intensified hydrological variability, yet the specific effects of pronounced hydrological changes on the transport and seaward fluxes of river pollutants remain unclear. To address this, this study utilized remote sensing hydrological station (RSHS) technology to obtain monthly runoff in the LRB. Combined with water quality monitoring data, the annual fluxes of total nitrogen (TN) and total phosphorus (TP) were calculated. Through correlation analysis, flux contribution decomposition, and ridge regression analysis, the relationships among changes in runoff, pollutant concentration, and pollutant flux were investigated, along with the influence of fluxes on estuarine chlorophyll-a (Chl-a) concentrations. New hydrological insights for the region This study first quantifies the "hydrological amplification effect" in the LRB. Climate-driven runoff significantly increased across all sub-basins (Mann–Kendall test Z > 1.96), driving sustained rises in seaward TN and TP fluxes. Runoff contributed 92–94% of flux changes, completely overwhelming emission reductions from decreasing local concentrations. This mechanism reveals that even with improved basin water quality, persistent runoff growth exacerbates estuarine eutrophication through enhanced scouring—31% and 27% of the Chl-a increase are attributable to TP and TN fluxes, respectively. Therefore, future environmental strategies must shift from concentration-based control to flux management and embed climate adaptation planning into integrated basin–estuary governance.

title: Rainfall and coastal water level relative timing as drivers of compound flooding in Haikou, China
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Guofeng Wu, Hanqing Xu, Laixiang Sun, Can Lu, Hayley J. Fowler, Patrick Willems, Jun Wang, Qing Liu, Yue Sheng
abstract: Study Region Urban area of Haikou, Hainan Province, China. Study focus Compound flooding in typhoon-prone coastal cities arises from the interaction between coastal water level and rainfall, but the role of their relative timing remains underexplored. This study proposes a framework that captures the relative timing for improved compound flooding assessment. Using the D-Flow FM model, we simulate 49 time-lag scenarios to quantify how timing ( ∆ t ) between coastal total water level and rainfall modulate inundation. For each scenario, we evaluate inundation volume and compute absolute ( ∆ M ) and relative ( ∆ R ) increments relative to the baseline. We delineate compound zones and decompose contributions from water level, rainfall, and their interaction. New hydrological insights for the region The results indicate that time-lags strongly shape compound flooding and produce nonlinear responses. Inundation is consistently larger when rainfall peaks before the coastal water level peak. A window from −19 h to −4 h yields volumes exceeding the historical event, and the maximum inundation occurs at −13 h with ∆ R = 9.44% and ( ∆ M = 8.53 million m³). Water level is the dominant driver, yet within compound zones, the interaction term exceeds rainfall alone. These findings highlight that taking ∆ t = 0 h as the worst-case can underestimate risks, emphasizing that the relative timing of rainfall and coastal water levels is a critical factor for managing compound flooding in coastal cities.

title: Determining the optimal groundwater depth for vegetation ecosystems in arid regions based on fuzzy comprehensive evaluation
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Rui Zhang, Jingwei Wu, Luguang Liu, Fengyan Wu, Wei Dong, He Wang, Jie Huang, Yibo Zhu
abstract: Study region The Hetao Irrigation District is an arid irrigation district in northern China where groundwater depth regulates natural vegetation in saline wastelands. Maintaining groundwater at an ecologically appropriate depth is important for balancing vegetation conservation and regional water management. Study focus This study developed a multi-level fuzzy evaluation system integrating vegetation structure and biodiversity indicators. A cloud model was used to quantify ecosystem quality across groundwater-depth gradients while accounting for fuzziness and randomness. Polynomial regression was used to characterize the relationship between groundwater depth and ecosystem quality. New hydrological insights for the region Ecosystem quality responded nonlinearly to groundwater depth. Depths of approximately 2–3 m produced the highest ecosystem-quality membership values and relatively low uncertainty, with peak performance near 2.5 m. Both shallower and deeper groundwater conditions were associated with reduced vegetation diversity and ecosystem quality. The 2–3 m range therefore provides a region-specific reference for coordinating ecological protection and groundwater regulation in the Hetao Irrigation District.

title: Abrupt shift in elevation-dependent snowmelt contribution in the Central Tibetan Plateau
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Zixiang Li, Hongyi Li, Weixin Xu, Yaru Yang, Rui He, Yiwei Liu, Yuanbao Feng, Na Dai
abstract: Study region The headwaters of the Yangtze River Basin on the Tibetan Plateau. Study focus This study examines whether the elevation dependence of snowmelt-driven runoff in a high-mountain basin can undergo an abrupt shift under recent climate warming. We apply a distributed hydrological model, constrained by streamflow observations and satellite-derived snow cover, to investigate changes in the elevation–runoff–snowmelt relationship over the past four decades. New hydrological insights for the region The results reveal an abrupt hydrological reorganization around the year 2000, when spring freezing-level height (H 0) reached ∼4750 m a.s.l., close to a statistically derived threshold (H crit = 4750 ± 150 m). After threshold crossing, elevation explained less variation in total runoff but more variation in snowmelt contribution. Basin-wide snowmelt contribution also shifted from a long-term increase to a sustained decline. This transition coincided with accelerated high-elevation warming, rising snowlines, reduced snowfall fraction, enhanced evapotranspiration, and thicker modeled active layers with increased baseflow. Climate reversion experiments indicate that the pre-shift regime can recover under cooler conditions, but only after a multi-year lag. These findings show that warming can trigger elevation-dependent hydrological threshold shifts in mountain basins and highlight freezing-level height as a useful diagnostic for detecting emerging changes in cryosphere-influenced headwaters.

title: Warming climate amplifies glacier hazards on the China-Pakistan Highway
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Chengde Yang, Xin Wang, Shichang Kang, Su Wang, Qiao Liu, Yong Zhang, Zhenfeng Wang, Junfeng Wei
abstract: Study region China–Pakistan Karakoram Highway (KKH) and its surroundings. Study focus Glaciers along the China–Pakistan International Karakoram Highway (KKH) exhibit relative stable or mass gain, a phenomenon termed “Karakoram Anomaly”, contrasting with widespread global glacier retreat. However, rising ice velocities and advancing termini are triggering more frequent glacier hazards, threatening infrastructure and communities. Despite these risks, a comprehensive assessment of their impacts on highway safety remains lacking. Here, we present a comprehensive assessment of potential ice avalanches (PIAs) and potential surging glaciers (PSGs) along the KKH over the past two decades, by combining machine learning techniques and statistical methods. New hydrological insights for the region We identified 344 PSGs and 1001 PIAs in 533 glaciers, primarily in the Karakoram and northeastern Pamir. These hazards pose catastrophic risks to 17 basins, directly affecting 25% basins, 68% local residents, 14 bridges, 154 attaching sites, and 130 km critical highway segments. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis reveals that terrain conditions, such as elevation, slope, and aspect, control PIAs, while climate warming significantly intensifies PSGs. It is projected to transit to a warming-wetting trend, signaling the weakening or even the end of the Karakoram Anomaly and leading to more frequent and severe glacier hazards. These findings highlight accelerating glacier instability under climate change and provide critical evidence for disaster prevention/mitigation strategies and infrastructure resilience in this region.

title: Environmental isotopes and multi-tracer evidence to elucidate deep groundwater circulation and fault-driven connectivity in complex karst systems: Case of the Middle Atlas, Morocco
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): F. Raibi, M. Maaziz, Y. Ait Brahim, M. Hssaisoune, H. Berrouch, H. Marah, M. Qurtobi, M. Benmanssour, T. El Ghali, M. Bellarbi, T. El Ghezlani, R. Essafi, L. Bouchaou
abstract: Study region The Middle Atlas Mountains in Morocco is a structurally complex karst where carbonate plateaus and major faults cut Liassic carbonates and Triassic evaporites, sustaining groundwater resources for adjacent semi-arid plains. Study focus A multi-tracer approach to constrain regional flow architecture, recharge elevation, groundwater age, and the processes controlling mineralization across unconfined and confined karst compartments. We combined major-ion hydrochemistry with environmental isotopes (δ²H, δ¹⁸O, ³H, and 14C) from 60 springs and 8 surface water sites, the study quantifies recharge elevations, groundwater residence times, and the geochemical drivers of mineralization in both unconfined and confined aquifer compartments. New hydrological insights for the region The study establishes the first massif-scale isotopic baseline, defining a new Local Meteoric Water Line (δ²H = 7.99 δ¹⁸O + 14.56) and a vertical δ¹ ⁸O gradient of −0.23‰ per 100 m, placing recharge altitudes between 700 m and 2490 m. Findings reveal a dual-flow system: fast-flowing conduit networks with modern water and confined compartments containing significantly older groundwater. Mineralization is primarily driven by subsurface Triassic evaporite dissolution. Furthermore, the Tizi N’Tretten fault zone is identified as a critical structural control facilitating vertical circulation and inter-basin flow, providing a vital framework for managing Mediterranean karst resources.

title: Physically consistent reconstruction and propagation analysis of droughts using a physics-informed neural network framework
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Tian Wang, Yongjiu Dai, Zhaoqiang Zhou, Xinjun Tu, Kairong Lin
abstract: Study region This study focuses on the Pearl River Basin, southern China, a humid yet seasonally variable monsoon basin where energy fluxes, water storage, and human management jointly influence drought onset, duration, and propagation. Study focus Current monitoring frameworks are predominantly empirical and tailored to specific indices, frequently overlooking the fundamental physical laws that maintain process consistency. Focusing on this challenge, this study presents a physics-informed neural network (PINN) that integrates both water-balance and surface energy-balance constraints within a deep learning framework to reconstruct a physically consistent Composite Drought Index (CDI) by fusing multi-source datasets. The index combines these meteorological, land-surface, and hydrological variables into a single latent space, enabling the derivation of drought intensity and evolution through percentile-based classification. New hydrological insights for the region Relative to unconstrained deep-learning baselines, the physics-guided PINN yields improved spatiotemporal coherence with a ∼9–15% reduction in reconstruction error. The research delineates representative drought archetypes, revealing that energy-limited residuals dominate short-term onset while water-storage deficits drive long-term propagation. Furthermore, the CDI demonstrates a critical 1–2 month lead time over traditional meteorological indices, providing an internally consistent representation for spatiotemporal tracking. This framework integrates physical conservation within a data-driven system, establishing a robust foundation for monitoring drought and diagnosing propagation in intricate hydro-climatic settings.

title: Optimal timescale of antecedent precipitation index for flood peak prediction in data-scarce mountain river basins
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Siming Li, Lu Chen, Bin Yi, Binlin Yang
abstract: Study region Two data-scarce mountain river basins in the Hanjiang River Basin, China: the Qinjiang River Basin (1578 km2) and the Hengshan Basin (12,624 km2). Study focus This study develops a data-driven dual-criteria framework (integrating elasticity and T statistic of correlation) to objectively optimize the antecedent timescale (AT) of the Antecedent Precipitation Index (API) for flood peak discharge prediction, addressing subjectivity in traditional API parameterization. The framework is applied to extensive historical flood events, and a Random Forest model incorporating AT-derived API and identified peak-producing rainfall is used to predict flood peak discharge. New hydrological insights for the region Quantitative analysis reveals that the hydrological impact of antecedent moisture conditions on flood peaks is maximized at specific, catchment-dependent timescales (ATopt = 16 days for Qinjiang River Basin, 13 days for Hengshan Basin), rather than the conventionally assumed 30-day period. This multivaluedness reflects fundamental differences in how basins regulate moisture storage and release; the optimal integration period is dictated by the interplay between basin physiography and the underlying runoff response mechanisms. By replacing arbitrary temporal assumptions with a dual-criteria framework that balances hydrological sensitivity and statistical robustness, this study advances the parameterization of antecedent precipitation. The resulting process-informed approach offers a transferable strategy to improve the accuracy and reliability of flood peak prediction across data-scarce mountain environments.

title: Can enhanced three-outlet diversion and joint lake-outlet regulation mitigate droughts in Dongting Lake, China?
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Xudong Zhang, Zongxue Xu, Chenlei Ye, Xinyi Shu, Xinyang Ma
abstract: Study region Dongting Lake (DTL), China. Study focus DTL, the second-largest freshwater lake in China and an internationally important wetland, has experienced increasingly severe droughts over the past two decades, posing serious threats to regional ecosystem stability and water supply security. Enhancing the diversion capacity of the three Yangtze River outlets to increase inflow to DTL has been proposed as a potential drought-mitigation measure. However, its effectiveness, potential adverse impacts, and synergy with other regulation strategies remain poorly quantified. To address these gaps, this study couples a hydrodynamic model with a two-stage hierarchical model proposed herein to systematically assess drought responses in DTL to enhanced three-outlet diversion and, for the first time, to quantitatively evaluate the drought-mitigation effectiveness and spatial complementarity of its joint implementation with a planned lake-outlet water-level regulation project. New hydrological insights The results indicate that (1) increasing diversion capacity markedly raises water levels in the West–South connecting channel, most areas of South DTL, and parts of the main drainage channel in East DTL, while slightly lowering water levels at the lake outlet and adjacent shallow areas. Accordingly, drought-mitigation effectiveness exhibits a pronounced spatial gradient, gradually weakening from West DTL to South DTL and then to East DTL. (2) Joint regulation effectively offsets lake-outlet water-level declines induced by enhanced diversion alone and substantially reduces drought duration, severity, and intensity at the lake-wide scale. Moreover, the two measures exhibit strong spatial complementarity: lake-outlet water-level regulation mainly mitigates droughts in East DTL and eastern South DTL, whereas West DTL and most areas of South DTL benefit primarily from enhanced three-outlet diversion. This study provides quantitative and mechanistic insights into coordinated drought management for DTL.

title: How sustainable land management practices may impact water resources in the Sahel: Insights from an integrated critical zone modelling approach
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Mahamadi Tabsoba, Basile Hector, Jean-Martial Cohard, Jean-Pierre Vandervaere, Aghali Ingatan Warzagan, Christophe Peugeot, Agnidé Emmanuel Lawin
abstract: Study region The study was conducted in the south-western Sahel of Niger, within a small experimental catchment of the AMMA-CATCH observatory characterized by degraded soils, short high-intensity rainfall events, and increasing implementation of sustainable land management (SLM) practices such as micro-dams. Study Focus This study investigates the hydrological impacts of SLM practices on runoff generation, soil water storage, and groundwater recharge using the integrated hydrological model ParFlow-CLM combined with field observations. The model was first calibrated under pre-intervention conditions using event-based runoff observations. Micro-dams were then introduced using equivalent Manning roughness coefficients calibrated against observations to represent their hydraulic effects on a Sahelian hillslope. New hydrological insights for the region Results show that the model reproduces the observed reduction in event-based runoff induced by SLM practices. Under the 8% managed-area scenario, corresponding to the 8% field implementation stage (0.64 ha over the modeled 8 ha hillslope), runoff coefficients decreased from 0.24 to 0.13 in observations and from 0.25 to 0.17 in simulations. Simulations also indicate enhanced infiltration and increased event-based soil water storage in the upper soil profile, reducing soil moisture stress during dry periods. Simulations suggest that hillslope-scale, diffuse groundwater recharge increased from about 15–17% of annual rainfall, while hillslope-scale runoff declined from 15% to 9%. These findings highlight the potential of SLM interventions to improve water availability and hydrological resilience in Sahelian environments.

title: Propagation and future projection of dry-wet abrupt alternation through the hydrological cycle using a GCM-VIC modeling framework
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Shuyou Liu, Jun Xia, Qianzuo Zhao, Xiaohua Xu, Ting Ye
abstract: Study region Poyang Lake Basin (PLB), a sub-region of the Yangtze River Basin in Southeast China. Study focus Climate variability and anthropogenic warming have intensified dry-wet abrupt alternation (DWAA) across many regions, posing growing challenges to regional and basin water resources management. However, the propagation patterns of DWAA through the hydrological cycle remain poorly understood. Using ensemble GCM-VIC simulations, the historical and future propagation processes of DWAA were simulated and projected in the PLB. Changes in cropland exposure to soil moisture DWAA were also compared. Propagation characteristics including propagation rate, lag time, and intensity response index were calculated for depicting meteorological-soil moisture DWAA propagation and meteorological-hydrological propagation under both historical and future scenarios. New hydrological insight (1) DWAA frequency and intensity will be higher under the SSP5–8.5 scenario than under SSP2–4.5. (2) Cropland exposure to DWAA events is projected to increase under future climate scenarios, particularly for dry-to-wet transition events. (3) Compared with historical scenarios, delayed propagation times and significant attenuate effects were observed during the DWAA propagation processes, especially under SSP5–8.5 scenario. These findings improve the understanding of DWAA propagation processes, providing useful references for water resource management and reducing risks of hydro-meteorological extremes.

title: Scale effects and time-lag responses of groundwater hydrochemistry to land use change: A spatiotemporal analysis of a rapidly urbanizing typical agricultural area in the Lower Yellow River alluvial plain
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Jiwei Feng, Min Zhang, Jianhua Ping, He Li, Jiaqi Liu
abstract: Study region Typical agricultural areas along the lower Yellow River in China Study focus Traditional assessments often overlook hydrochemical spatial heterogeneity and spatiotemporal land-use lags. Utilizing datasets (1985–2010), this study reconstructs groundwater evolutionary trajectories. We developed an improved SOM-PMF (Self-Organizing Map and Positive Matrix Factorization) model for refined source apportionment, and a SOM-RF-SHAP framework to evaluate scale-dependent and lagged associations between land-use predictors and groundwater chemistry. New hydrological insights for the region Groundwater hydrochemical evolution followed a non-linear Natural Baseline-Pulse Disturbance-System Recovery trajectory. High-intensity human activities (1991–2000) triggered sharp increases in sulfate and total dissolved solids (TDS), shifting groundwater toward sulfate-enriched Ca-Mg/Na hydrochemical facies, with pronounced recovery signals emerging only after 2006. By integrating SOM-based hydrochemical classification with PMF source apportionment, the SOM-PMF model captured multivariate hydrochemical patterns and revealed clear spatial heterogeneity. This approach identified three interpretable source factors-carbonate weathering, cation exchange, and anthropogenic mixed inputs. Furthermore, SOM-RF-SHAP revealed distinct scale-dependent and lagged land-use responses. High-mineralization areas showed strong local, long-lag responses, with cropland most strongly associated with TDS (SHAP = 599.7; 500 m; 7 years), consistent with cumulative agricultural salinization. Carbonate weathering–cation exchange mixed areas showed a broader, shorter-lag sulfate response to impervious surfaces (SHAP = 67.5; 1 km; 4 years), whereas low-mineralization areas showed weak land-use explanatory power.

title: Response of terrestrial water storage to climate warming-wetting in Northwest China
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Xinyang Yan, Qiang Zhang, Wen Chen, Jinhu Yang, Ping Yue, Qinping Xiao, Lili Bao, Rong Wang, Yongmao Peng
abstract: Study region Northwest China (NWC). Study focus Terrestrial water storage is a crucial component of the water cycle and a major water source for both human activities and the maintenance of a stable ecological environment. As climate warming-wetting intensify in NWC, it is increasingly urgent to analyze the spatio-temporal evolutions of Terrestrial Water Storage Anomaly (TWSA) and its components in this region, as well as their response to climate change. Using high-precision grid data we systematically analyzed the response characteristics of TWSA and its components to climate warming-wetting in NWC, and revealed the relative contributions of climatic factors to TWSA variations. New hydrological insights The TWSA has undergone distinct phase change: an initial increase, followed by fluctuations around the baseline, and then a sharp decline since 2013. The overall decline in NWC TWSA is evident. Both Soil Moisture Storage Anomaly and Canopy Water Storage Anomaly have shifted from negative to positive anomalies around 2016, and the Groundwater Storage Anomaly has turned negative since 2013. The evapotranspiration is the major driving factor of TWSA, and precipitation plays a secondary but prominent regulatory role. Human activities play a dominant role in TWSA variations, accounting for approximately 60.51% with a predominantly negative contribution and exceeding the impact of climate change. This study can provide a scientific basis for water resource management, ecological restoration and sustainable development in NWC.

title: Hybrid ICEEMDAN-VMD-LSTM framework for probable maximum drought estimation along the Lower Yangtze River Basin
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Chao Lv, Longcang Shu, Hao Ke, Xiaoran Yin, Long Zhou, Chengpeng Lu, Bo Liu
abstract: Study region Zhenjiang City in Jiangsu Province, China—representative riparian city in the lower Yangtze River Basin Study focus We propose an integrated model that incorporates parameter optimization through the Crested Porcupine Optimizer (CPO), dual-signal decomposition using Improved Complete Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition with Adaptive Noise (ICEEMDAN) and Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD), and a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network for long-term forecasting of the Standardized Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI). During the long-term forecasting process, dynamic error compensation is incorporated to mitigate the error accumulation inherent in recursive forecasting, while preserving intrinsic stochastic characteristics of hydrological time series, and the probable maximum drought (PMD) is subsequently estimated. New hydrological insights for the region The ensemble model demonstrates better long-term prediction performance than the standalone LSTM model, preserving the statistical and volatility characteristics in the original data. Future PMD events substantially surpass historical extremes across multiple indicators, with intensity increasing by at least 17% and duration exhibiting a maximum increase of up to 282%. Although the precise timing of PMD occurrences remains highly stochastic, statistical results indicate that the occurrence of future droughts still exhibits periodicity, suggesting that the future regional climate system still maintains an underlying rhythmic structure. This study provides an effective framework for PMD estimation and offers a valuable method for regional water resource planning and drought emergency management under changing climate conditions.

title: Topographically informed satellite monitoring of reservoir storage: A multi-regional evaluation across contrasting hydroclimatic settings
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Ignacio Fuentes, Federico Campos, Rafael Navas, R. Willem Vervoort
abstract: Study region The study evaluates four reservoirs located in Europe (Spain), South America (Chile), Australia, and North America (USA), representing contrasting hydroclimatic and morphometric conditions. Study focus Reliable monitoring of reservoir storage is essential for water allocation and drought preparedness. However, many regions lack consistent in-situ observations or high-resolution bathymetry. This study develops a topographically informed optimisation framework that departs from conventional sequential workflows by jointly coupling spectral water delineation and elevation-derived inundation within a single objective function. Water-index thresholds and inundation levels are simultaneously optimised by minimising discrepancies between satellite-derived water masks and elevation-constrained flooded surfaces. The framework was tested across reservoirs with contrasting morphometry (from steep canyon systems to shallow floodplain lakes), storage dynamics, and climatic conditions, and compared against fixed and histogram-based thresholding approaches. New hydrological insight for the region The proposed framework consistently improves storage estimation across diverse hydroclimatic settings by enforcing hydraulic consistency between spectral delineation and topographic constraints. Results show that elevation representation dominates estimation uncertainty, accounting for more than 89% of variability, while spectral threshold selection plays a secondary role. The method remains robust under moderate elevation data degradation, supporting its application in data-scarce regions where reservoir morphology is reasonably represented. These findings highlight the importance of integrating topographic information into satellite-based reservoir monitoring and provide a transferable approach for improving water storage assessment across contrasting regional environments.

title: A XGBoost-based composite drought index combining multi-source remote sensing data for drought monitoring in China
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Xing Huang, Xianghu Li, Yani Song, Zhenhe Lv, Ligang Xu, Dan Zhang
abstract: Study region China. Study focus The composite drought index (CDI) is crucial for monitoring and evaluating drought, which can overcome the limitations of single indicators and provide a more comprehensive depiction of drought evolution. This study integrated multi-source data based on the XGBoost to construct a monthly-scale CDI at the national scale and analyzed the spatiotemporal patterns of drought in China from 2001 to 2020. New hydrological insights for the region The CDI showed stable performance across contrasting climatic and land-surface conditions and was able to reflect both meteorological drought signals and soil moisture stress. In representative drought events, it provided a more coherent depiction of drought evolution than single-source indices. At the national scale, the CDI revealed marked spatiotemporal heterogeneity of drought in China: drought was generally most severe in autumn, with the highest severity (1.67) and the longest duration (3.44 months), whereas spring showed the lowest drought severity (1.17). Spatially, Inner Mongolia (IM) and Northeast China (NEC) emerged as the main drought-prone regions, with persistently high severity in IM (1.57–1.99). These findings indicate that integrating multi-source drought signals within a machine-learning framework can improve national-scale drought monitoring in China and provide a stronger basis for region-specific drought-risk assessment and early warning.

title: A Bayesian framework for non-stationary magnitude-frequency modeling of debris flows under environmental change in Jiangjia Gully
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Yilong Yu, Jinbo Tang, Chen Liu, Tao Wang, Chunhao Wu, Xubo Jia, Can Yang
abstract: Study region This study focuses on the Jiangjia Gully in Yunnan Province, China. Based on 319 observed debris flow events from 1961 to 2024, the long-term field dataset is adopted for statistical analysis. Study focus Accurate quantification of debris-flow magnitude-frequency relationship is critical for hazard risk assessment and disaster mitigation. Traditional models generally neglect environmental change effects on such relationship. This study proposes a novel methodological framework by integrating extreme value theory with Bayesian techniques. The innovative coupling of Bayesian change-point detection and segmental modeling enables reliable identification of temporal evolution characteristics of debris-flow magnitude-frequency under changing environments, effectively addressing the inherent limitations of conventional non-segmented models. New hydrological insights for the region The Generalized Pareto Distribution (GPD) performs well in fitting debris flow magnitude distribution of Jiangjia Gully. A significant change point occurred around 2002 with an obvious decline in debris flow frequency. Full-sample non-segmented models overestimate event magnitude and fail to capture regime shifts. The established stage-specific model well depicts variations in return period and level. Vegetation restoration tends to be the dominant driver, compared with rainfall and seismic activity. The proposed framework supports non-stationary frequency analysis and provides reliable references for debris flow risk assessment and engineering design in mountainous hazard-prone areas.

title: Capability assessment of the novel hybrid MCDM GIS-based approaches and machine learning algorithm for flood hazard analysis in South of Iran
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Karim Solaimani, Shadman Darvishi
abstract: Study region Southern Baluchistan basin, Iran. Study Focus Presenting new methods is one of the essential steps in developing a methodology for flood occurrence, which is a crucial measure in environmental planning for effective flood management. In this study, the capability of several hybrid approaches, including extended fuzzy-pivot pairwise relative criteria importance assessment (Fuzzy PIPRECIA), fuzzy-combined compromise solution (FuzzyCoCoSo), weighted aggregated sum product assessment (WASPAS), ordered weighted average (OWA), and complex proportional assessment (COPRAS), was investigated to prepare flood hazard maps (FHM). Furthermore, the vulnerability of land use categories (LUC) in FH conditions and flooded LUC was evaluated using Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 images and the Random Forest algorithm. New hydrological insights for the region: The Fuzzy PIPRECIA model, with a Spearman rank correlation coefficient of 0.8393, and the new hybrid MCDM, with an average ROC-AUC coefficient of more than 0.81, had very good and excellent performances for FHM preparation. Based on the FuzzyCoCoSo, FuzzyPIPRECIA-FuzzyCoCoSo-OWA, FuzzyPIPRECIA-WASPAS and FuzzyPIPRECIA-COPRAS models, about 34.40% (16,712.69 km2), 41.20% (20,014.48 km2), 48.50% (23,562.26 km2), and 31.54% (15,323.25 km2) of the southern Baluchistan basin are in very high and high FH conditions, 29.67%, 31.06%, 36.14% and 34.82% are in medium FH, and 25.99%, 20.24%, 17.18% and 33.59% are in low FH conditions, respectively. Additionally, the 2019 and 2022 floods in the southern parts resulted in damage to rangeland (1056.47 km²), bare ground (477.96 km²), built areas (6.17 km²), and crops (16.15 km²). These situations demonstrate the critical flood condition and the demand for appropriate flood management planning in the southern Baluchistan basin.

title: Response of gross primary productivity to compound drought–heat events in southeast asian rubber plantations
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Qinggele Bao, Lan Wu, Yongfang Wang, Rihan Su, Ziqin Wang, Zhenghong Tan, Licong Dai, Peng Wang, Enliang Guo, Zhongyi Sun
abstract: Study Region The Southeast Asian rubber belt (SEA-RB) spans mainland and maritime Southeast Asia (SEA), encompassing approximately 14.2 million hectares of rubber plantations. Study Focus This study quantified compound drought–heat events (CDHEs) across SEA-RB from 2001 to 2020 using a Compound Drought–Heat Index (CDHI) and investigated their impacts on gross primary productivity (GPP) through integrated remote sensing analysis and structural equation modeling (SEM). Novel Hydrological Insights for the Region We identified five major sustained CDHEs that strongly coincided with ENSO phases. Intensification hotspots emerged in mainland SEA (42.72% of plantations), particularly within the northwestern Indochinese Peninsula, whereas maritime regions remained stable. CDHEs caused progressive GPP losses (56% ± 3.2–61% ± 5.2%), significantly exceeding single-stress scenarios. SEM analysis revealed that CDHEs strengthen stomatal regulation as the dominant control on photosynthesis while substantially mitigating direct thermal damage to enzymatic processes. This protective trade-off prioritizes hydraulic safety over carbon assimilation, a mechanism absent under isolated stressors. These findings demonstrate that compound extremes trigger qualitatively distinct physiological responses, highlighting the inadequacy of single-stressor approaches for predicting and managing tropical plantation productivity under future climate scenarios.

title: Fine-scale canopy architecture and rainfall partitioning in karst vegetation: Evidence for a capture-and-funnel redistribution pattern from terrestrial laser scanning
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Siyuan Peng, Yanqing Li, Ziwen Yang, Yiming Wang, Junling Jin, Linyan Pan, Yingjie Sun
abstract: Study Region The Karst Critical Zone in Southwest China is characterized by limited surface-water retention and high susceptibility to soil erosion, both increasingly intensified by frequent high-intensity rainfall events. In this fragile landscape, understanding how forest canopies redistribute rainfall is important for water-resource management and ecological restoration. Study Focus This study integrated Terrestrial Laser Scanning (TLS) with event-based ecohydrological monitoring of three species (Bischofia javanica, Bauhinia variegata, and Taxodium distichum) to examine how fine-scale three-dimensional canopy structure influences rainfall partitioning. Based on 30 rainfall events monitored from January to June 2025 (710.8 mm), linear mixed-effects models were used to evaluate the roles of canopy traits and event-scale meteorological conditions in regulating throughfall, stemflow, and interception. New Hydrological Insights for the Region Results revealed interspecific ecohydrological divergence in rainfall partitioning, indicating that canopy structural variation and event-scale meteorological forcing shaped rainfall redistribution beneath karst vegetation. An intensity-dependent, threshold-like shift in rainfall redistribution was observed, suggesting joint effects of canopy structure and rainfall intensity. Taxodium distichum exhibited a more pronounced "Capture-and-Funnel" strategy, with lower cumulative throughfall (59.01%) and greater stemflow concentration (7.21%), whereas the broad-leaved species were more throughfall-dominated, with Bischofia javanica reaching the highest cumulative throughfall rate (70.80%). These findings suggest that denser canopies may enhance rainfall buffering and internal flow reorganization, with implications for soil protection, localized infiltration, and species evaluation in karst ecological restoration.

title: Vegetation greening in arid Northwest China may exacerbate water scarcity risks
description: Publication date: August 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 66 Author(s): Chang Lu, Qiang Zhang, Philippe Ciais, Long Ma, Tingxi Liu, Gang Wang, Deliang Sun, Vijay P. Singh, Yungang Bai, Zhenlin Lu, Bolin Sun, Xing Huang
abstract: Vegetation plays a critical role in modulating the water cycle via transpiration. Therefore, understanding how vegetation interacts with terrestrial water storage (TWS) across space, time, and soil depth is essential for developing sustainable water-resource strategies in arid regions. A major challenge is that vegetation–water relationships in drylands are highly heterogeneous, nonlinear, and often lagged, making it difficult to identify when greening alleviates or intensifies water stress. Nevertheless, the spatiotemporally heterogeneous and coupled relationships between vegetation and TWS in these areas remain poorly understood.
